summary.headline: Hexagon Nutrition FY26 revenue rose 17.8% to INR382.63 crores, EBITDA margin expanded to 13.83% and PAT grew 56.1% to INR37.94 crores.
summary.overview: This was the maiden earnings call after the company's NSE and BSE listing, covering Q4 and FY26 results. Management reported FY26 revenue of INR382.63 crores (up 17.8%), EBITDA of INR52.90 crores (up 32.01%) and PAT of INR37.94 crores (up 56.1%). Q4 revenue was INR115.04 crores, Q4 EBITDA INR15.35 crores (13.34% margin) and Q4 PAT INR10.9 crores (9.5% margin). Management attributed margin gains to branded product mix, premix growth and manufacturing efficiencies, and guided to continued margin expansion, though much of the call was qualitative and some figures were stated loosely.

financial_highlights.change: vs about INR60 crores last year

segments.name: Branded / clinical and consumer nutrition (PentaSure, PediaGold, Obesigo)
segments.commentary: About 30% of FY26 revenue per CFO, with gross margins cited at 60-68%; operates at 50-60% utilisation. Management says it expanded from roughly 10% of revenue to 30%.

segments.name: Micronutrient premixes (B2B to pharma and FMCG)
segments.commentary: About 35-40% of FY26 revenue; EBITDA margin guided at 35-40%; utilisation around 40-45%. Premix domestic order jump was dispatched largely in Q4.

segments.name: ESG segment (RUTF, RUSF, micronutrient powders)
segments.commentary: About 30% of FY26 revenue; margin guided at 25-30%; utilisation 35-40%, sometimes up to 60%, depending on order flow. Large orders dispatched in Q4 added to receivables.

guidance_outlook: Management expects to maintain the growth momentum of the last two to three years and some margin expansion as operating leverage improves.
Blended capacity utilisation expected at 35-40% for year-end and going forward, up from 30% (figure cited as YTD December).
Management said revenue growth aspiration over 3-5 years is roughly a doubling of the business, consistent with the past four to five years (CEO-level confirmation: 'correct estimate').
Management said West Asia war has not significantly hurt business and it expects to continue its growth journey in FY27; Q1 may be affected, per analyst framing.
Tender-based (UN) business has a healthy order pipeline, so utilisation is expected to improve over time.
capex_capacity: Blended capacity utilisation about 30% per presentation (YTD December), expected to reach 35-40% for year-end; branded 50-60%, premix 40-45%, ESG 35-40%.
Management said it keeps a capacity buffer for future tenders and unanticipated orders.
Manufacturing sites in Nashik (Maharashtra) and Chennai (Tamil Nadu MEPZ-SEZ). Wholly owned subsidiaries in South Africa, India, Uzbekistan and Hong Kong.
Analyst referenced chronic underutilisation of 37% cited in the DRHP, attributed to UN tenders; no capex amount or commissioning timeline was given.
Management said it will strengthen manufacturing capabilities where required but gave no capex quantum.
demand_pricing: Exports are about 57% of revenue; more than 80% of exports come from premixes and ESG, with the balance from branded exports. West Asia is under 20% of exports.
Imports are under 25% of raw material requirements, mainly vitamins (A, B-group, C, folic acid) from China, Singapore, Korea and Europe. No significant sourcing challenges reported.

Clinical nutrition market size cited at about INR6,300 crores; management says the company is a small share. Growth plans include more medical representatives, Tier 2/3 expansion, e-commerce (Amazon, Flipkart, e-pharmacies) and medical marketing.
Whey price increase handled by passing it through to MRPs in branded; vitamins are hedged via strategic inventory. No major impact so far.
Competitors in premixes: DSM, Firmenich, BASF, SternVitamin, Piramal. In branded, MNCs Abbott, Nestle and Fresenius Kabi. Management declined to give a market share figure.

qa_highlights.question: Split of export revenue by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: More than 80% of exports come from premixes and ESG; the balance is branded exports. Brand names were not disclosed as customer permissions were not obtained.

qa_highlights.question: Margin trajectory and what drove EBITDA margin from 6.2% to 13.8% over four years?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said branded products (gross margin above 50%) were the main driver, with premixes adding support and growing about 20-30% over four years.

qa_highlights.question: Volume growth and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to maintain recent momentum and expand margins by segment: branded 60-68%, premix 35-40%, ESG 25-30%.

qa_highlights.question: Utilisation outlook and UN tender dynamics?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended utilisation of about 30% is YTD December; expected at 35-40% for year-end. Tender business has a healthy pipeline, so utilisation should improve.

qa_highlights.question: Rise in trade receivables from INR60 crores to about INR82 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Driven by large ESG orders dispatched in the last quarter and a domestic premix order jump dispatched mostly in Q4; management says these have normalised.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 export growth outlook given West Asia war?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the war has not negatively affected the business and it expects to continue the growth journey, with no quantified FY27 guidance.

risks_watch: Receivables jumped to about INR82 crores from INR60 crores; watch for normalisation and collection days in FY27.
Raw material exposure: imported vitamins (under 25% of inputs) and whey price volatility; pass-through only in branded.
Geopolitical risk: West Asia accounts for under 20% of exports; Q1 FY27 impact possible.
Low blended utilisation (about 30%) and reliance on lumpy UN/tender orders make volume and absorption uncertain.
Competition from DSM, BASF, Firmenich, Piramal in premixes and Abbott, Nestle, Fresenius Kabi in branded; brand penetration of PediaGold and Obesigo is low.
Management did not quantify FY27 revenue or margin guidance and gave no capex plan.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on structural nutrition demand and margin story, but evasive on quantified guidance, market share and capex. Several answers were generic or qualitative, and some numbers (such as utilisation and segment shares) were given inconsistently or with caveats.
key_quotes: Revenue from operations increased by 17.8% year-on-year to INR382.63 crores.
EBITDA increased by 32.01% to INR52.9 crores, while EBITDA margins expanded to 13.83%.
Nutrition today is no longer viewed as a supplementary product; it has become an essential component of healthcare.
So, we expect to maintain the same momentum what we have created in the last two to three years from the guidance point of view I can say that.

growth.why: Management expects to maintain the last 2-3 years' growth momentum and utilisation rising from ~30% to 35-40% by year-end, with a tender pipeline and Tier 2/3, e-commerce and medical rep plans, but no capex quantum, commissioning timeline or specific capacity additions were given.
